comparisons.peer_summary: Net revenues increased 16% to $53.51 billion in 2024, driven primarily by higher revenues in Global Banking & Markets (Equities, Investment banking, FICC) and Asset & Wealth Management (Equity investments, Management fees), with slight increases in Platform Solutions.
comparisons.comparison: GS confirms the trend of increased investment banking fees driving segment revenue growth, consistent with BAC's 31% increase. GS reports that net revenues in Global Banking & Markets were higher primarily due to 'significantly higher Investment banking fees,' alongside higher Equities and FICC revenues. While BAC specifies the drivers (debt/equity issuance and advisory), GS highlights the magnitude ('significantly higher') as a key component of its overall 16% net revenue growth, corroborating the strong market conditions described by BAC and JPM.

sentences.text: Total Corporation investment banking fees, which exclude self-led deals and are primarily included within Global Banking and Global Markets, increased 31 percent to $6.2 billion compared to the same period in 2023 primarily due to higher debt and equity issuance fees and higher advisory fees.
Net revenues were $53.51 billion for 2024, 16% higher than 2023, primarily reflecting higher net revenues in Global Banking & Markets and Asset & Wealth Management.

The increase in net revenues in Global Banking & Markets primarily reflected higher net revenues in Equities, significantly higher Investment banking fees and higher net revenues in Fixed Income, Currency and Commodities (FICC).

comparisons.peer_summary: Investment banking fees increased in 2024 due to favorable market conditions, resulting in higher debt underwriting fees from increased leveraged loans and bond issuances, higher equity underwriting fees from IPO and follow-on offerings, and higher advisory fees from increased M&A activity.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM attribute their 2024 investment banking fee increases to favorable market conditions driving higher debt and equity issuance, as well as advisory activity. BAC reports a 31% increase to $6.2 billion, citing higher debt and equity issuance fees and advisory fees. JPM reports a 37% increase in Investment Banking fees, specifically noting higher debt underwriting fees driven by leveraged loans and bonds, higher equity underwriting fees from IPOs and follow-ons, and higher advisory fees from increased M&A activity. Both firms identify the same primary drivers: underwriting (debt/equity) and advisory.

sentences.text: Total Corporation investment banking fees, which exclude self-led deals and are primarily included within Global Banking and Global Markets, increased 31 percent to $6.2 billion compared to the same period in 2023 primarily due to higher debt and equity issuance fees and higher advisory fees.
Investment banking fees increased, reflecting in CIB the benefit of favorable market conditions, which resulted in:
• higher debt underwriting fees predominantly driven by higher industry-wide issuances in leveraged loans, and in high-grade and high-yield bonds,
• higher equity underwriting fees driven by higher industry-wide fees and wallet share gains in IPOs, and in follow-on and convertible securities offerings, and
• higher advisory fees driven by higher industry-wide mergers and acquisitions ("M&A") activity and wallet share gains.

comparisons.peer_topic: Investment Banking Revenue Growth and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Investment banking net revenues increased 35% to $6,170 million in 2024, driven by higher M&A advisory volumes, increased equity underwriting from IPOs and follow-ons, and higher fixed income underwriting from bond and loan issuances.
comparisons.comparison: MS reports a 35% increase in investment banking net revenues to $6.17 billion, aligning closely with BAC's 31% increase to $6.2 billion in structure and drivers. Like BAC, MS attributes growth to higher underwriting and advisory revenues. Specifically, MS cites higher M&A advisory volumes (matching BAC's 'higher advisory fees'), higher equity underwriting from IPOs and follow-ons (matching BAC's 'higher... equity issuance fees'), and higher fixed income underwriting from bond and loan issuances (matching BAC's 'higher debt... issuance fees').

sentences.text: Total Corporation investment banking fees, which exclude self-led deals and are primarily included within Global Banking and Global Markets, increased 31 percent to $6.2 billion compared to the same period in 2023 primarily due to higher debt and equity issuance fees and higher advisory fees.
Net revenues of $6,170 million in 2024 increased 35% compared with the prior year, reflecting an increase in underwriting and Advisory revenues.
• Advisory revenues increased primarily due to higher completed M&A transactions.
• Equity underwriting revenues increased primarily on higher initial public offerings and follow-on offerings.
• Fixed income underwriting revenues increased primarily reflecting higher bond issuances, non-investment grade loan issuances and securitized products revenues.
